rationale: The agent correctly authenticated the user via full name + zip and operated only on the user’s orders. It identified the correct laptop order and found the requested variant, and it modified the wristwatch variant correctly. However, it performed multiple order-changing writes without explicitly stating the exact changes and obtaining the user’s confirmation beforehand, which violates policy: (1) modified the laptop configuration immediately after the user listed desired specs; (2) modified the wristwatch variant after saying it would check and update, without seeking explicit confirmation; (3) attempted to update the shipping address without confirmation. Additionally, it disclosed and mischaracterized the NYC address as being in the user’s profile (user details showed only the Houston address; the NYC address appeared on a past order), and it revealed the full address despite the user’s stated preference not to share it. When the address update failed due to order status, the agent appropriately offered a handoff and completed the transfer. Because of the lack of required confirmations and the inaccurate claim about the address location, the conversation does not meet the pass bar.
